How to resize a signature image to pixels and KB

By Sarvesh Singh · Updated 20 October 2026

A portal can require both exact image dimensions and a file-size range. These are separate checks: a 300 × 100 pixel JPG is not automatically 20 KB. The file size also depends on image detail, format and encoding quality.

Start with the portal’s instructions

Write down the accepted format, width, height and minimum/maximum file size. The example below uses 300 × 100 pixels only to explain resizing; it is not a specification for any exam or authority. Use the current instructions for your own application.

Worked example: 1,000 × 400 to 300 × 100

Our practice image is a 1,000 × 400 pixel drawing labelled SAMPLE, not a real signature. Its aspect ratio is 2.5:1, while the example output is 3:1.

  • Fit: the entire drawing scales to 250 × 100 pixels inside the 300 × 100 output, leaving 25 pixels of space on each side.
  • Centered crop: approximately 33 pixels are removed from the top and bottom of the source before scaling to 300 × 100. Real handwriting near those edges could be cut off.

For a signature, first check Fit. Choose Crop only when you can keep every pen stroke within the crop area. Do not stretch the image simply to fill the box.

  1. Open Resize signature image and select the practice PNG or your own permitted image.
  2. Enter the portal’s actual pixel dimensions and file-size range. Check whether it defines KB as 1,000 bytes or uses a binary size convention.
  3. Choose an accepted format. JPG can reduce size using lossy encoding; PNG is lossless but may be larger.
  4. Choose Fit or adjust the crop, then process the image.
  5. Review the preview and resulting dimensions/size. Download and inspect the final file before uploading it to the portal.

Why the target KB range may be impossible

A clean signature on a plain background may already be smaller than a portal’s stated minimum. Adding meaningless padding would only disguise the issue, so this tool does not do it. Conversely, a detailed image may exceed a very small maximum even at the lowest quality the tool tests. The tool reports the problem instead of secretly changing your requested dimensions.

Final checks

Use Check image requirements to compare the downloaded file with the requested dimensions, format and size. Check that handwriting is legible, the background meets the instructions and no strokes were cropped. This tool resizes an existing image; it does not create a legally binding electronic or digital signature.

Image input is limited to 12 MiB, 24 megapixels and 12,000 pixels on either side. Use a supported JPG, PNG or still WebP source. For general images, try Resize an image.
